prior_exception.reason: The defining 120 EC in years one and two is chemistry and laboratory centred: analytical, organic and inorganic chemistry; molecular structure and bonding; thermodynamics, quantum mechanics and physics; successive chemical synthesis and analysis laboratories. In year three, at least 12 EC of chemistry electives and a 12-EC independent chemistry research internship/report remain required. Although 27 EC can be freely chosen, UCR lacks a chemistry gateway and any stand-alone introductory or advanced organic, inorganic, analytical, physical or synthetic chemistry sequence. A 24-course UCR route using biology, geoscience, statistics and programming would have too little chemistry and would misrepresent the programme’s academic core.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The official prospective year-one page is labelled 2027–28 while the year-two and year-three pages are indicative 2026–27; these are a present programme structure cross-check, not a guaranteed cohort contract. Summing positive-credit items yields 60 EC in each year. Year-three 9 EC taught compulsory work plus 12 EC compulsory internship plus 39 EC elective room = 60 EC; 12 of the latter is restricted to Chemistry electives, with 27 EC free. The education minor is optional, and alternative chemistry electives are not simultaneously required.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Checked all 151 enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, profile/topic enrichment, prerequisites and planned terms. HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry and HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory provide biochemical content and molecular lab work, while HCBGATE101 and HCBLIFE211 introduce life science and cells. ENSENVI311 Environmental Biogeochemistry and ENSDELT311 R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation touch geochemical/inorganic processes and recovery; ENSSUST112 and ENSSUST211 address materials life cycles and energy systems. DISGATE102, DISMATH211/214/314 and DISGATE101 provide some mathematical, statistical and programming support. None provides the laboratory and theory progression in chemical analysis, organic/inorganic synthesis, physical chemistry, molecular spectroscopy and quantum chemistry required to underpin this bachelor and its independent chemistry research internship. Isolated biochemical and environmental chemistry coverage cannot support a defensible 24-course Chemistry match.

prior_exception.reason: Aerospace Engineering is a tightly sequenced professional engineering degree. Its compulsory spine combines calculus, differential equations, probability, physics, engineering mechanics, materials and structures, aerospace design and construction, aerodynamics with wind-tunnel testing, structural and vibration analysis, flight and orbital mechanics, propulsion and power, signals and control, numerical modelling, aerospace systems engineering and production, flight dynamics and flight testing, and a 15-EC aerospace Design Synthesis Exercise. UCR offers useful mathematics, programming, numerical methods, linear systems, statistics, AI, robotics, sustainability and general product-design courses. It has no equivalent progression in classical mechanics, aerospace materials and structures, fluid mechanics and aerodynamics, propulsion, orbital mechanics, aircraft stability and flight dynamics, aerospace production, wind-tunnel and flight-test practice, or integrated aircraft/spacecraft design. The available quantitative and computational courses can support an engineering-adjacent liberal-arts pathway, but cannot form a defensible Aerospace Engineering comparator.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The current 2026-2027 Implementation Regulations confirm the complete 180-EC structure: a 60-EC first-year major, 60-EC second-year major, 30-EC minor, 15-EC third-year major and 15-EC Design Synthesis Exercise. The official pre-2027 curriculum chart accounts for those credits course by course. Year one develops aerospace orientation and engineering drawing, introduction to aerospace engineering, materials and structures, statics and dynamics, two calculus courses, physics, linear algebra, Python scientific computing and a 9-EC aerospace design-and-construction module. Year two advances system design, subsonic and supersonic aerodynamics with wind-tunnel testing, structural and vibrational analysis, differential equations, probability and statistics, test/analysis/simulation with aerospace AI, flight and orbital mechanics, propulsion and power, aerospace signals and control, and numerical analysis and computational modelling. Year three combines a 30-EC minor with systems engineering, aerospace design and production, flight dynamics and simulation with flight testing, and the 15-EC Design Synthesis Exercise.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide relevant quantitative foundations. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISDATA211 Machine Learning, DISDATA311 Neural Networks & Deep Learning and DISDATA312 Robotics add programming, AI and computational applications. BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design offers team design, quantitative modelling, fabrication and prototyping; ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design add energy and wind-related sustainability contexts. These are meaningful adjacent courses, but the workbook contains no university physics sequence for engineers, statics-and-dynamics sequence, mechanics of materials, aerospace materials, structural analysis, vibration engineering, fluid mechanics, subsonic or supersonic aerodynamics, wind-tunnel laboratory, thermodynamics and propulsion, flight mechanics, orbital mechanics, aircraft stability and flight dynamics, aerospace telecommunications and instrumentation, flight-test laboratory, aerospace manufacturing and production, or integrated aircraft and spacecraft systems design. DISMATH312 covers mathematical representations of linear systems rather than the target's full aerospace signals, control and flight-dynamics formation; DISDATA312 covers robot kinematics and motion planning rather than aircraft dynamics or aerospace control; and BENENTR111 is general consumer-product development rather than load-bearing aerospace design and certification practice. UCR also lacks a 15-EC capstone equivalent to AE3200 in which the complete aerospace design process synthesises these technical disciplines. The target's defining engineering-science, experimental and design sequence therefore remains overwhelmingly unmatched.
